findings.title: Security incident in November 2026
findings.summary_md: Todoist’s advisory says an attacker used a stolen version-control credential between November 22 and 23, 2026 to modify workflows in three repositories and reach its cloud infrastructure. It reports an export of email addresses, account creation dates and salted SHA1 password hashes for approximately 6% of users, API and Slack tokens for approximately 0.003%, and credential-like content or Outlook mailbox data for approximately 0.001% in each smaller group. The company says it blocked access, rotated exposed internal credentials, retired SHA1 support and protected affected accounts; its update log records initial publication at 16:11 UTC on November 24.

findings.title: Todoist Discloses Breach Affecting User Records and Connected Accounts
findings.summary_md: CXO Digitalpulse reported that Todoist’s incident notice said a stolen development credential was used on November 22 and that production access followed on November 23. The account export covered approximately 6% of users and contained email addresses, account creation dates and salted SHA1 password hashes, not plaintext passwords. The report also described token exposure for approximately 0.003% of users and credential-like task content and Outlook mailbox excerpts for approximately 0.001% in each group.

findings.title: Todoist breach: old SHA1 password hashes for about 6% of users taken, plus API, Slack and Outlook data for a few. What to do
findings.summary_md: TechMeasured traced the intrusion from a stolen version-control credential through automated workflows in three repositories to cloud infrastructure, citing Todoist’s November 24 incident report. It reported the roughly 6% legacy salted SHA1 hash exposure and the smaller API, Slack, task-content and Outlook groups, and noted Todoist found no application-code changes or sign-ins to the SHA1 accounts. The article advised affected users to reset disabled passwords, rotate API tokens and revoke credentials stored in Todoist content.
